question.text: After a call for help from this city by Alexius Angelus, the objective of the Fourth Crusade was changed from attacking Egypt to sacking it.
question.clue: A road called the mese (MEH-say) ran through this city, which may have lost forty percent of its population in a plague in 542 CE. A gigantic cannon designed by Orban sufficed to break through this city's 60-foot-tall Theodosian Walls.

swap.leadin: Procopius wrote a lively, if historically and logically dubious, account of this man's reign.
swap.text: Name this Byzantine emperor and husband of Theodora who sought to reconquer the Western Roman Empire. He also constructed the Hagia Sophia.
swap.clue: He expelled pagan teachers from the Academy in Athens.

question.leadin: During this event, rioters attempted to crown Hypatius as the Byzantine emperor, but were massacred in the Hippodrome by Belisarius.
question.text: Those rioters, members of the Blue and Green demes, orchestrated this event named for their chants of "Victory!"
question.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

swap.text: This legal code passed by Justinian is sometimes named after him, and is composed of three main parts with a minor fourth section. The Codex and Digest are two of those sections.
swap.clue: For centuries, scholars puzzled over how three million lines were reduced to 150,000 during this work's creation.

question.leadin: The 1274 Second Council of Lyon was an unsuccessful attempt to resolve this event.
question.text: Name this 1054 event which permanently divided the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
question.clue: Disputes over whether leavened or unleavened bread should be used in the Eucharist and the supremacy of the Pope led to this event.

swap.text: Khan Tervel of Bulgaria formed an alliance with the second emperor of this name in 704. The first Byzantine emperor with this name ordered the rebuilding of the Hagia Sophia (AI-uh SOF-yuh) and the recompilation of laws.
swap.clue: Before his first overthrow, he lost the Battle of Sebastopolis to the Umayyads, after which this ruler ordered the butchering of all the Slavs in Bithynia.

question.text: This general helped put down the Nika Riots with Mundus and Narses. This general led the campaigns against the Vandals and the Goths under Justinian the Great.
question.clue: He was ordered to depose Pope Silverius in favor of Vigilius, an act for which he later repented, and he married Antonina, a court favorite who wielded a good deal of influence.

swap.text: A supporter of the Blues, this Byzantine emperor was nearly overthrown in the Nika riots. He promulgated a legal code and his queen was Theodora.
swap.clue: This major Byzantine emperor codified Roman law with his namesake law code and sent his general Belisarius to reconquer Italy from barbarian tribes which had overrun the Roman empire

question.leadin: The Triumph of Orthodoxy engineered by Theodora largely ended support for this position.
question.text: Identify this stance once popular in the Byzantine Empire wherein many "graven images" were removed from Orthodox churches.
question.clue: The first attempt to apply this doctrine officially was met with resistance at the Chalke Gate, and it was condemned by the Second Council of Nicaea convoked by Irene.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the wonderful world of wartime weaponry.
swap.text: This Byzantine ruler was described as inventing several types of trebuchets during the 1097 Siege of Nicaea. This ruler's request of aid from Europe triggered the First Crusade, and his daughter Anna wrote a notable biography of him.
swap.clue: Although one rival was forced to give up his territorial gains to assist Henry IV, that rival, Robert Guiscard, defeated this man's forces at the Battle of Dyrrachium.

question.leadin: All of this crusade's members were excommunicated when they left to attack Zara for the Venetian doge Enrico Dandolo.
question.text: Identify this crusade that never reached Jerusalem and instead attacked Christian lands.
question.clue: Boniface of Montferrat was made King of Thessalonica as a result of this conflict, whose aftermath saw the creation of the Latin Empire.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the 1453 conquest of Constantinople by the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: The death of Constantine XI during the battle brought an end to the two hundred year rule of this final dynasty of Byzantine emperors.
swap.clue: This dynasty's founder wedded his daughter into the noble family of Trebizond; that founder was Michael VIII. Its last ruler, Constantine XI, died in the Ottomans' siege of Constantinople.

question.text: This elite group of Norse fighters in the Byzantine army was formed when Basil the Bulgar-Slayer had his sister Anna married off to Vladimir the Great in exchange for their service.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.text: Disputes with the Byzantines over monastic funding partly convinced Tamar to install a ruler of this name as the first emperor of Trebizond. An earlier Komnenian king of this name called for assistance from the Crusaders against the Seljuk Turks.
swap.answerHtml: Alexios [or Alexius; accept Alexios I Megas Komnenos of Trebizond; accept Alexios I Komnenos]
swap.clue: One Byzantine ruler of this name sent emissaries to the Council of Piacenza in order to seek military aid. An account of that ruler with this name's reign was published by Anna Komnene, the daughter of that ruler.

question.text: Before becoming emperor, Constantine ruled this despotate that encompassed much of the Peloponnese peninsula whose capital was Mystras.
question.clue: At that time, the entire Peloponnese was under the control of this Despotate, which had been established circa 1349 by Byzantine emperor John VI Cantacuzenus, and then taken over by the Palaeologus dynasty. It was ruled from a site near ancient Sparta.

swap.leadin: A cadet branch of this dynasty ruled the Italian duchy of Montferrat.
swap.text: Identify this house whose members included Manuel II, who was controversially quoted by the Pope in 2006, and Michael VIII, who ascended to the throne after expelling the Latin Empire from Constantinople.

question.text: This woman wrote admiringly of the manly traits of Empress Irene in her influential Byzantine history, The Alexiad.
question.clue: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.

swap.text: Some people believe that Hereward fled to the employ of the fifth Count of Flanders to bear this name, which he shared with two Kings of Jerusalem who followed Godrey of Bouillon and reigned from 1100 to 1131.
swap.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

question.leadin: This clash took place near modern-day Konya, and the victory of the winning side is generally attributed to their ability to occupy the elevated position.
question.text: Identify this 1176 battle in which the forces of the Sultanate of Rum, led by Arslan II, inflicted an overwhelming defeat on the Byzantine army.

swap.leadin: This ruler, who introduced jousting and other Western European traditions to his kingdom, was hailed as a chivalric model by contemporaries, such as his chronicler John Kinnamos.
swap.text: Identify this grandson of Alexius I, a Byzantine emperor who attempted an alliance with the papacy under Adrian IV. His attempt to regain Anatolia was halted at the Battle of Myriokephalon.
swap.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.
